items.title: Pay invoice for painting work
items.quote: Bitte überweisen Sie den Betrag innerhalb von 14 Tagen nach Erhalt dieser Rechnung auf unser Konto.
items.computation: The payment period is 14 days 'nach Erhalt dieser Rechnung' (after receipt of this invoice), not from a fixed invoice date. The letter shows no invoice date/Rechnungsdatum at all - only the completion date of the work (12.08.2026) and the invoice number are printed. Because this is a private commercial invoice, not a letter from a public authority, the statutory 3-day delivery fiction (e.g. §122 AO, §41 VwVfG) does not directly apply; receipt is governed by §130 BGB (actual arrival in the recipient's sphere and normal reading time). Without knowing when the invoice was actually sent/received by Frau Beispiel, the start of the 14-day period, and hence the exact due date, cannot be reliably determined. If one assumes (only as a rough illustration) that the invoice was sent shortly after the work was finished, e.g. around 12.08.2026-14.08.2026, and reached her a few days later, the 14-day period would already have elapsed well before today (2026-09-25). Given the missing date, the due date is left unresolved and the person should check the date actually printed on their copy of the invoice or the postmark/email date to compute 14 days from that receipt date.

warnings: The invoice itself carries no date (no 'Rechnungsdatum'), only the work-completion date (12.08.2026); without knowing the actual date of issue/receipt, the 14-day payment deadline cannot be computed exactly — please check the date shown on your original copy, the postmark, or the email that delivered this invoice.

This is a private invoice from a tradesperson, not from a public authority, so the statutory delivery-fiction rules used for official mail do not strictly apply; the payment period runs from actual receipt under §130 BGB.
